what: which rung to drive next, ordered by what its reading would be WORTH rather than by how much mass it adds. A trajectory scores d_k = w_k - w_0 driven by our gradient, so a section whose single-step gradient already sits near the zero-gradient baseline cannot produce a trajectory reading that carries information -- it can only saturate.
why_this_exists: the obvious order is by mass, which puts pairformer_stack (+5.8282) first. That is also the most expensive rung (11.41 h, FLOOR.json) and, frame-matched, the one whose gradient is nearest saturation. Checking the static readings first cost minutes and reordered 11.41 h of box time.

the_baseline_every_reading_is_against.source: perf/of3t_trunkg043/SCORE_c64.json A16_zero_gradient_baseline, measured not asserted, exactly_one true. A reading of 0.9 against this is not a pass.

diffusion_module.amplification_static_to_trajectory: the diffusion arm's static gradient is 0.0079 (conditioning) to 0.1167 (transformer) mass-weighted against float64, and its 20-step trajectory reads 0.2564. So a 20-step trajectory reads LARGER than the single-step gradient it is driven by, roughly 2.2x here, because the error accumulates and because d_k differences two small quantities. That factor is what makes a static reading near 1.0 a refusal rather than a warning.

candidate_rungs_in_the_order_TO_DRIVE_TH.verdict: DRIVE FIRST. The lowest mass-weighted gradient error of any section in the model against float64, 0.00231 with cos 1.00000, and 180 of 244 tensors compared. A small module with no 48-noise-level sample axis, so cheap.
candidate_rungs_in_the_order_TO_DRIVE_TH.caveat: its MEDIAN over tensors is 1.01520 while its MASS-WEIGHTED reading is 0.00231, so the section's mass sits in a few tensors that agree almost exactly while the typical tensor is at saturation. A15/D17 in miniature. A trajectory scores rel_d over the CONCATENATION, which is the mass-weighted quantity, so this rung is the right one to drive -- but its per-tensor picture must be reported beside the headline, not instead of it.

AMENDED_2026-09-22_pass2.what_was_wrong: this entry ranked aux_heads first on 0.0023114566 mass-weighted against float64 and explained its MEDIAN of 1.01520 as mass concentration, A15/D17 in miniature. The concentration is real but it is NOT what puts the median at 1.0. The mechanism is a MISSING MASK, and the arm that shows it existed before this row started.

the_arm_pair.source: perf/of3t_auxgrad/grad_M_masked.json and grad_N_unmasked.json, of3t-auxgrad's re-take of instrument A at aux scope, 176 tensors, same reference, same boundary

AMENDED_2026-09-22_pass2.what_the_pair_says: the MASS-WEIGHTED reading is insensitive to the mask -- 0.002271 masked against 0.002300 unmasked, a 1.3 % difference -- while the MEDIAN over tensors moves 19.5x, 0.05366 to 1.04818, and the count over the per-tensor bar goes 89 to 171 of 176. The FORWARD decides it: masked, 0 of 5 heads are over bar with a worst of 0.00505; unmasked, 4 of 5 are over bar with pae_logits at 0.51771. PROTOCOL A18's first clause is that a disagreeing forward invalidates the gradient taken at it, so the unmasked gradient is taken at a forward that disagrees.
AMENDED_2026-09-22_pass2.which_number_the_campaign_carries: MODEL_d56_retake.json's aux_heads figure comes from perf/of3t_auxheads/aux_instrument.py via scoperun.sh, which passes no --mask and whose instrument has no such flag. So the 0.00231 the campaign carries -- and that this entry ranked on -- is arm N, the unmasked one. of3t-auxgrad's own docstring says of that arm's 2.2996e-03: 'the gradient of a different function'.
AMENDED_2026-09-22_pass2.why_the_ranking_SURVIVES_anyway: a trajectory scores rel_d over the CONCATENATION, which is the mass-weighted quantity, and that quantity is the same to 1.3 % under both masks. So aux_heads is still the right rung to drive first. What changes is HOW: it must be driven with the masks ON, and the unmasked arm must be run beside it as the control, because otherwise the trajectory is seeded by a forward that disagrees with upstream on 4 of 5 heads and the reading cannot be attributed.

live_tree_check.forward_device_signature: forward_device(self, si_input_d, si_trunk_d, zij_trunk_d, oh_d, use_zij_trunk_embedding=True, pair_mask_d=None, attn_mask_d=None)
live_tree_check.status: the mask repair from of3t-auxfind IS landed and IS plumbed, and both arguments DEFAULT TO NONE -- the source comment says so outright: 'Both default to None, so the shipped default is unchanged and every existing caller computes the same function.' A landed lever at default off is not a landed win.
live_tree_check.who_calls_it: the only tt_bio call site is openfold3_confidence.py:387, the inference s_path=='device' branch, and it passes no masks. _S_PATH_DEFAULT is 'host', so inference does not reach it by default either. The source states 'Training does not read this -- it calls forward_device directly', and there is NO shipped training caller of the confidence head in tt_bio.
live_tree_check.consequence: the mask setting for a training trajectory at aux scope is a HARNESS choice, not a shipped-code fact. Neither arm can be called 'the shipped trajectory'. So this row runs BOTH and says which is which, rather than picking one and naming it shipped.

AMENDED_2026-09-22_pass2.the_general_error_to_note: the mechanism was retrodicted. A15/D17 concentration FITS a median near 1.0 and is a real property of this section, so it read as an explanation; the arm that actually moves the median by 19.5x was already on disk in a sibling namespace. Naming a plausible mechanism is not measuring one.

candidate_rungs_in_the_order_TO_DRIVE_TH.verdict: DRIVE SECOND. 0.08915 mass-weighted against float64, comparable to the diffusion_transformer's 0.11670 that already sits inside a working trajectory, and its median over tensors is 0.02709, better behaved than aux_heads.
candidate_rungs_in_the_order_TO_DRIVE_TH.caveat: 154 of 227 tensors compared, so 0.0083 % of model mass inside the section has no device gradient and stays out of scope.

candidate_rungs_in_the_order_TO_DRIVE_TH.source: perf/of3t_frame384/FRAME_N384.json MATCHED.ours_vs_REF_LOCAL_f64_n384, crop 384, FRAME-MATCHED: our arm against the local float64 reference taken at the same boundary, not against the model-frame bundle. The cross-frame reading in the same file is 2.1595 and would be the wrong number to use here.
candidate_rungs_in_the_order_TO_DRIVE_TH.verdict: DEFER, and not on cost. Frame-matched at crop 384 this arm reads 0.8354 mass-weighted against float64, where the zero-gradient baseline is exactly 1.0 and 2735 of 2736 tensors are over the per-tensor bar. Applying the ~2.2x static-to-trajectory amplification the diffusion arm exhibits, a 20-step trunk trajectory would read at or above saturation, so the 11.41 h would buy a number that says 'saturated' and nothing more.
candidate_rungs_in_the_order_TO_DRIVE_TH.what_would_change_it: the trunk's SINGLE-STEP gradient error has to come down first. of3t-frame384's own leaf attribution puts 93.80 % of the failure on LayerNorm affine; that is a porting target, and it is cheaper to measure at one step than at twenty.
candidate_rungs_in_the_order_TO_DRIVE_TH.do_not_read_the_c64_numbers_as_this: SCORE_c64.json reads 5.5069 (SHIPPED) and 9.0252 (FLIPPED) at crop 64. Those are a different padded width AND a different arm configuration from the crop-384 frame-matched 0.8354. Quoting either as 'the trunk arm' would repeat the cross-frame error this campaign has already made once on this exact section.

what_this_does_to_the_reachable_ceiling.note: 92.1567 %, which is the static instrument's ENTIRE coverage (92.1568 %, MODEL_d56_retake.json). So the two cheap low-error rungs take the trajectory to the static instrument's own reach, and the expensive high-mass rung is the one that would saturate. 97.9849 % still needs the trunk, and the trunk needs porting first.
